paragraphs: Shabbetai son of Rabbi Marinus. (A Yerushalmi, in the time of Rabbi Chiyya.)[^1] In Bava Metzia 17 it is related that he promised his daughter-in-law a fine wool cloak in her marriage contract. Her marriage contract was lost. He said, ‘There was never any such obligation.’ Witnesses came—he said to them, ‘I paid it.’ He came before Rabbi Chiyya, who told him, ‘You have been shown to have falsely denied the obligation concerning that cloak.’[^2]

From [Beitzah 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.32b.3), it appears that he was a distinguished man. It is related there that he came to Babylonia and asked them for business funding, but they did not give it to him; nor did they provide him with food. He said, ‘These people descend from the mixed multitude, for it is written: “He will grant you compassion and have compassion on you.” Whoever shows compassion to others is known to be descended from our father Abraham,’ etc.

notes.text: Yerushalmi may mean a sage of the Land of Israel rather than specifically a resident of Jerusalem. The proofread name is מרינוס (Marinus); the older OCR has מריגום.
The marriage contract is a ketubah. Hyman cites Bava Metzia 17 without specifying a side of the folio.
